newsitem.title: FRANCE: Former French ministers accused in asbestos suit.
newsitem.headline: Former French ministers accused in asbestos suit.

text.p: A former French shipyard worker with lung disease has filed a lawsuit accusing eight ex-cabinet ministers of failing to protect him from asbestos exposure, the man's attorney said on Sunday.
The lawsuit names six former health ministers dating back to 1986 as well as two other ministers responsible for guarding against major technological risks, lawyer Maryse Joissains told Reuters.

The suit, filed in a special high court which hears only cases against top-level officials such as cabinet members, alleges the ministers knew of the health risks of asbestos exposure yet failed to take action to regulate it.
The worker's name was not released.
"The dangers of asbestos have been know for more than 30 years. Protective measures should have been adopted long ago," said Joissains.
She has previously pressed similar charges on behalf of haemophiliacs allegedly infected with AIDS due to France's delay in ordering the screening of blood donations for the AIDS virus.
French prosecutors agreed for the first time earlier this month to allow a legal complaint that blamed a cancer on occupational exposure to asbestos to go to trial .
But that case, involving electrician Jean Dalla Torre, 64, did not identify state officials it believed to be responsible for the exposure, instead asking a court to fix the blame.
France announced recently that it was banning virtually all uses of asbestos from January 1, 1997, long after action by most other industrialised nations against the substance.
It took the step following publication of a scientific report estimating that 2,000 people would die in France this year from contact with the industrial fibre.
Commonly used as an insulation material in the construction industry until the 1970s, asbestos was linked by scientists decades ago to lung cancers and other lethal respiratory ailments.
